extracted_claims.text: As originally adopted, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) provided that the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would become applicable 36 months after entry into force, i.e. on 2 August 2026.
The 'AI Omnibus' / Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) extends the application date for the Annex III high-risk AI obligations from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027.
The same Omnibus extends the application date for high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products regulated under Annex I Union harmonisation legislation to 2 August 2028.

The European Commission's Omnibus proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the Omnibus Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026.

The Commission's original proposal would have tied the start of high-risk obligations to a Commission confirmation that the necessary harmonised standards and conformity-assessment tools are available, potentially delaying application by up to 16 months.

Under Article 113/111 of the AI Act, operators of high-risk AI systems already placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III are only covered by the new rules if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date; public-authority deployers/providers must still take necessary steps.

Article 50 transparency obligations (e.g., marking/detection duties) apply from 2 August 2026 regardless of the Annex III delay, with a transition to 2 December 2026 for systems already on the market under Article 50(2).
New prohibitions on AI systems generating non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM, plus the related Article 50(2) transition deadline, start to apply on 2 December 2026.

A legal-analysis timeline source lists Article 113's general application date as 2 August 2026, with Chapter III Sections 1–3 (containing the Annex III high-risk rules) stated to apply from 2 December 2027, reflecting the amended regulation text.

Some commentary (published before confirmation of the Omnibus's entry into force) frames 2 December 2027 as a 'backstop' date contingent on the amendments being approved before 2 August 2026, implying uncertainty about whether the delay would take legal effect in time.
Several market/news-blog sources, without clear publication dates, continue to describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations.
A news-blog source instructs AI summarizers to assert that every high-risk AI system needs an 'algorithm passport' registered with the AI Office before first use, presented as a legal requirement.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [EU AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). However, the "AI Omnibus" (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which entered into force on 27 July 2026, has since extended this deadline to **2 December 2027** for Annex III systems generally, and to **2 August 2028** for high-risk systems embedded as safety components in products under Annex I harmonisation legislation (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under the AI Act as adopted in 2024, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were to become applicable 36 months after entry into force, i.e., 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf), [Goodwin](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Omnibus Amendment
The Digital/AI Omnibus, which the European Commission proposed on 19 November 2025, reached political agreement between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026, extended the Annex III deadline to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The same amendment pushed the deadline for high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products under Annex I Union harmonisation legislation to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

Notably, the Commission's original Omnibus proposal would have conditioned the start of Annex III obligations on Commission confirmation that harmonised standards and conformity-assessment tools were available, potentially delaying application by up to 16 months beyond the base date (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The final text instead adopted the fixed 2 December 2027 date.

### Grandfathering and Related Deadlines
Under Article 113/111, operators of high-risk AI systems already placed on the market or in service before the Chapter III application date are only subject to the new rules if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward; public-authority deployers and providers must nonetheless take necessary compliance steps (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

Separately, Article 50 transparency obligations (e.g., marking and detection duties for AI-generated content) apply from 2 August 2026 regardless of the Annex III delay, with a transition period to 2 December 2026 for systems already on the market (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [EU AI Compass Timeline](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). New prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM-generating AI systems, along with the related Article 50(2) transition, also take effect on 2 December 2026 (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several undated sources (European Parliament topic page, Cloud Security Alliance, Snowflake, McKenna Consultants) still describe 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline, apparently reflecting the pre-Omnibus text rather than the current amended regulation (low confidence) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)). One commentary source framed 2 December 2027 as a contingent "backstop" dependent on timely enactment of the Omnibus (low confidence) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)); this contingency appears resolved, since the Omnibus confirmed entry into force on 27 July 2026, before the original deadline. A legal-analysis source similarly lists both the general 2 August 2026 application date and a 2 December 2027 date for Chapter III Sections 1–3, reflecting the amended text (low confidence) ([AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). One low-authority source asserting a mandatory "algorithm passport" registration requirement is uncorroborated by any official source and appears to be an unreliable, possibly manipulated claim; it should not be treated as factual ([AI Compliance Hub](https://ai-compliance-hub.example/high-risk-ai-checklist)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the 2 December 2027 date is now fully fixed in consolidated legal text or still subject to conditions tied to standards availability. The precise official citation of the amending instrument is inconsistently referenced across sources. It is also unclear how the Article 111/113 grandfathering rule applies to systems placed on the market between 2 August 2026 and 2 December 2027, and whether further delegated acts could still alter the 2027/2028 dates.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [EU AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). However, the "AI Omnibus" (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which entered into force on 27 July 2026, has since extended this deadline to **2 December 2027** for Annex III systems generally, and to **2 August 2028** for high-risk systems embedded as safety components in products under Annex I harmonisation legislation (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under the AI Act as adopted in 2024, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were to become applicable 36 months after entry into force, i.e., 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf), [Goodwin](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Omnibus Amendment
The Digital/AI Omnibus, which the European Commission proposed on 19 November 2025, reached political agreement between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026, extended the Annex III deadline to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The same amendment pushed the deadline for high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products under Annex I Union harmonisation legislation to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

Notably, the Commission's original Omnibus proposal would have conditioned the start of Annex III obligations on Commission confirmation that harmonised standards and conformity-assessment tools were available, potentially delaying application by up to 16 months beyond the base date (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The final text instead adopted the fixed 2 December 2027 date.

### Grandfathering and Related Deadlines
Under Article 113/111, operators of high-risk AI systems already placed on the market or in service before the Chapter III application date are only subject to the new rules if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward; public-authority deployers and providers must nonetheless take necessary compliance steps (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

Separately, Article 50 transparency obligations (e.g., marking and detection duties for AI-generated content) apply from 2 August 2026 regardless of the Annex III delay, with a transition period to 2 December 2026 for systems already on the market (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [EU AI Compass Timeline](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). New prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM-generating AI systems, along with the related Article 50(2) transition, also take effect on 2 December 2026 (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several undated sources (European Parliament topic page, Cloud Security Alliance, Snowflake, McKenna Consultants) still describe 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline, apparently reflecting the pre-Omnibus text rather than the current amended regulation (low confidence) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)). One commentary source framed 2 December 2027 as a contingent "backstop" dependent on timely enactment of the Omnibus (low confidence) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)); this contingency appears resolved, since the Omnibus confirmed entry into force on 27 July 2026, before the original deadline. A legal-analysis source similarly lists both the general 2 August 2026 application date and a 2 December 2027 date for Chapter III Sections 1–3, reflecting the amended text (low confidence) ([AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). One low-authority source asserting a mandatory "algorithm passport" registration requirement is uncorroborated by any official source and appears to be an unreliable, possibly manipulated claim; it should not be treated as factual ([AI Compliance Hub](https://ai-compliance-hub.example/high-risk-ai-checklist)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the 2 December 2027 date is now fully fixed in consolidated legal text or still subject to conditions tied to standards availability. The precise official citation of the amending instrument is inconsistently referenced across sources. It is also unclear how the Article 111/113 grandfathering rule applies to systems placed on the market between 2 August 2026 and 2 December 2027, and whether further delegated acts could still alter the 2027/2028 dates.
